label: Product Hunt
terms_note: Free; GraphQL at https://api.producthunt.com/v2/api/graphql; OAuth2 client-credentials token for public reads, authorization code with scopes public private write for user context; 'partial write access to third party applications depending on the use-case' granted by request (hello@producthunt.com) — no mutation to create a Post / launch is offered; PH 'reserves the right to rate-limit any application' (fair use; complexity-based limits per token).

capabilities: write(partial — by request: follows, goals; no post creation)

reference.verdict: **Verdict** — has_api: **partial** (GraphQL read API; write only by arrangement, no launch creation).
auth: 1. Create an application at producthunt.com/v2/oauth/applications (API dashboard) → client id / secret.
2. Read-only public data: `POST /v2/oauth/token` with `grant_type=client_credentials` → developer token.
3. User context: authorization code with scopes `public private write`; "partial write access to third party
reference.limits: - Fair-use rate limiting ("we reserve the right to rate-limit any application"); complexity-based quota per token (headers `X-Rate-Limit-Limit / Remaining / Reset`). - Launch creation is UI-only (scheduled by the maker/hunter); Product Hunt community rules forbid vote solicitation and fake engagement.

fields.name: token
fields.help: Product Hunt API token: the non-expiring developer_token of your application in the API dashboard (https://www.producthunt.com/v2/oauth/applications), or an OAuth user token with scopes public private; sent as 'Authorization: Bearer {token}' (https://api.producthunt.com/v2/docs).

adapter.envelope_note: GraphQL failures arrive as HTTP 200 {data: null, errors: [...]} and become error results.
adapter.terms: Read-only by default ('By default all apps are read-only'); 'The Product Hunt API must not be used for commercial purposes' without permission (hello@producthunt.com); fair-use rate limiting (https://api.producthunt.com/v2/docs).

body.query: =query { viewer { user { id username name headline url } } }

me.note: Query.viewer (needs a user-context token: the developer_token or an OAuth user token; a client-only token has no viewer) returns account.data.viewer.user {id, username, name, headline, url}.

body.query: =query($id: ID!, $first: Int!) { post(id: $id) { comments(first: $first) { totalCount edges { node { id body createdAt url user { username } } } } } }

read_comments.note: Post.comments(first, order NEWEST) of the post with id `post_id` (numeric Product Hunt post id; Query.post also takes a slug, not mapped). Cursor-paginated: only the first `limit` comments (max 20 here) are returned and `page` is not honoured; top-level comments only (replies are Comment.replies).

body.query: =query($id: ID!) { post(id: $id) { id name url votesCount commentsCount reviewsRating featuredAt } }

analytics_post.note: Launch counts of one post: votesCount, commentsCount, reviewsRating and featuredAt as top-level fields (no views in the API). An unknown id answers data.post = null, reported as invalid_input.

not_offered.publish_text: The API has no mutation that creates a post or launch; its mutations are goal* and userFollow* only (type Mutation in https://github.com/producthunt/producthunt-api/blob/master/schema.graphql), and 'partial write access' is granted case by case (https://api.producthunt.com/v2/docs).
not_offered.publish_image: No post-creation or media-upload mutation exists (type Mutation in https://github.com/producthunt/producthunt-api/blob/master/schema.graphql).
not_offered.reply_comment: No comment mutation exists (type Mutation in https://github.com/producthunt/producthunt-api/blob/master/schema.graphql: goalCheer, goalCreate, goalUpdate, userFollow ...).
not_offered.read_mentions: The schema has no mentions or notifications query (type Query in https://github.com/producthunt/producthunt-api/blob/master/schema.graphql).
not_offered.delete: No delete mutation for posts or comments exists (type Mutation in https://github.com/producthunt/producthunt-api/blob/master/schema.graphql).

evidence: host api.producthunt.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (Google Trust Services)
probe: 3/3 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
spec https://raw.githubusercontent.com/producthunt/producthunt-api/master/schema.graphql: 3/3 tools match (path, method, parameters, body keys, response paths)
